about: Probe bank for exam mode (docs/js/examiner.js). Hand-written. kind: trap = asked when the answer box or a number in the transcript matches a computed trap answer with this tag (docs/data/checks.json); question = tied to questions by skills, interpretation kinds, ids or number of tables; trigger = asked when the transcript or answer box matches one of the triggers (regular expressions, case-insensitive); generic = asked when nothing else applies. topic: Excel, SQL, Regression or any. pushback: said once when the answer to this probe is thin.

grain.label: Wrong grain
grain.hint: Before you aggregate, say what one row of the data represents and what one row of your answer should represent.

key.label: Non-unique key
key.hint: Check whether the value you look up or count by is unique in that column. If it is not, what else identifies a row?

join.label: Rows duplicated by a join
join.hint: After a join, count the rows. If the count went up, the join key is not unique on one side.

ratio.label: Average of ratios
ratio.hint: An average of rates weights every row equally. Is that what the question asks, or is it total over total?

confound.label: Confounding
confound.hint: A coefficient shows an association in this data. Think about what else differs between the groups or days you compare.

population.label: Wrong population
population.hint: Say your filter out loud: which rows are in, and does that match the group the question names?

definition.label: Wrong definition
definition.hint: Read the question's definition again, word by word, and compare it with what your formula or query counts.

boundary.label: Boundary or parsing
boundary.hint: Check the edges: values exactly on a limit, codes written in more than one way, and how dates and text are parsed.

probes.text: Does your count include the same album twice? What does one row in your result represent?
probes.pushback: Say what one row is before the count, and what it should be.

probes.text: What does one row in the data you used represent? Is that the level the question asks about?
probes.pushback: Be specific. One row is one what? And one row of your answer is one what?

probes.text: If you summed or averaged directly over the rows, would a day with many rows count more than a day with few?
probes.pushback: Walk me through how the rows add up to the number you gave.

probes.text: Is the value you looked up or counted by unique in that column? How do you know?
probes.pushback: How would you check that in the file, right now?

probes.text: Did every row count equally in your average? Should a row with two hours count as much as a row with forty?
probes.pushback: So is the average of the rates the same as total over total here? Why or why not?

probes.text: Which rows did you include? Say your filter out loud and compare it with the question.
probes.pushback: Which group does the question name, exactly?

probes.text: Read the question's definition back to me. Does your number count exactly that, nothing more and nothing less?
probes.pushback: Which part of the definition did your formula or query leave out or add?

probes.text: What happens at the edges? Values exactly on the limit, codes written in another way, and how the dates or text were parsed.
probes.pushback: Take the boundary value itself. Is it in or out, and why?

probes.text: What is the grain of the result after your join? Can the join duplicate rows?
probes.pushback: Which side of the join could have more than one match per key?

probes.text: Is the value you look up unique in the lookup column? What happens if it is not?
probes.pushback: Which match would VLOOKUP return if there were two?

probes.text: After grouping, what does one row represent?
probes.pushback: One row is one what, and why is that the level the question needs?

probes.text: Is your figure an average of ratios or a ratio of totals? Which one does the question want?
probes.pushback: Why does the difference matter here?

probes.text: Distinct on which columns? Is one column alone enough to identify a row?
probes.pushback: How would you prove there are no hidden duplicates?

probes.text: Say your condition out loud. Which rows are in and which are out?
probes.pushback: Does that match the group the question names?

probes.text: How did you turn that text or date into something you can compare? What could go wrong for some rows?
probes.pushback: Give me one row where your method would fail.

probes.text: Walk me through the equation with the numbers in. Is every input inside the observed range?
probes.pushback: Why does it matter whether the input is inside the observed range?

probes.text: What is the null hypothesis, and at what level are you testing it?
probes.pushback: So what does that p-value let you say, and what does it not let you say?

probes.text: Would you read that coefficient as a cause? Could a third variable explain the relationship?
probes.pushback: Name one variable that is not in the model and could drive both.

probes.text: Compared with which group? And do game days differ from other days in ways the model does not see?
probes.pushback: Name one thing that differs on game days apart from the game.

probes.text: Why that lookup and not another? Is the value you look up unique?
probes.pushback: What would happen with a duplicate in the lookup column?

probes.text: What is the grain of the result after that join? Can it duplicate rows?
probes.pushback: How would you check the row count before and after?

probes.text: Is an average of percentages the same as the overall percentage here?
probes.pushback: Which rows get more weight in one than in the other?

probes.text: What does one row represent now?
probes.pushback: One row is one what?

probes.text: Which field is your key in that pivot, and is it unique?
probes.pushback: What would the pivot do with two rows that share the key?

probes.text: Distinct on which columns? Is that column alone a key?
probes.pushback: Could two different things share that value?

probes.text: Say your filter out loud. Which rows are in, and which are out?
probes.pushback: Does that match the group the question names?

probes.text: Is the boundary value itself included? Check the wording of the question.
probes.pushback: Take a row exactly on the limit. In or out?

probes.text: Does that count include blanks or missing values? Should it?
probes.pushback: What does a blank mean in this column?

probes.text: Could a third variable explain that relationship?
probes.pushback: Name one variable that is not in the model and could move both.

probes.text: Significant at which level? And what does that p-value tell you, in plain words?
probes.pushback: What would you tell a partner who asks whether the effect is big?

probes.text: What does R squared tell you here, and what does it not tell you?
probes.pushback: Does a low R squared make the coefficients wrong?

probes.text: What is the reference group for that dummy, and is the comparison fair?
probes.pushback: What else is different about those days?

probes.text: Why did you do it that way?
probes.pushback: That tells me what you did. Why?

probes.text: What would you check to be sure the number is right?
probes.pushback: Give me one concrete check you could do in the file.

probes.text: How would you explain this result to a partner who does not use Excel?
probes.pushback: Say it in one sentence, without the formula.

probes.text: Is there another way to get the same number? Would you trust it more or less?
probes.pushback: Why more, or why less?

lines.thin_gentle: Can you say a bit more?
lines.thin_default: That tells me what you did. Why?
lines.time_up: Time is up. Let us stop there.
